Subject: Request: DPA addendum for EU data residency & security annex

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re preparing a procurement package for Acme Payments where Redwood will be the inference provider. Two quick asks up front so Legal/Security can triage:

- We need a DPA addendum that explicitly covers EU data residency for customer-controlled datasets and a TOMs annex that documents encryption, key management, and access controls.
- We’d like clarity on BYOK options: can Redwood support customer-managed keys hosted in our EU KMS, and do you allow key escrow or key-holding by Redwood?

I’ve attached an initial redline to your standard DPA (Acme_DPA_v2_redlines.docx) and a short TOMs request (TOMs_Annex_request.pdf). High-level preferences: 30-day subprocessor notice, no key escrow, SCCs for transfers, and SOC 2 Type II evidence plus latest pen test summary.

Can you confirm whether these are feasible and, if so, who at Redwood should be on the technical call to scope the TOMs edits? We’re hoping to close procurement in the next 10 business days.

Best,
Jane Sullivan
Sr. Counsel — Data Privacy
Acme Payments

Subject: Re: Request: DPA addendum for EU data residency & security annex

Jane —

Thanks for the clear redlines and TOMs request. We can support the majority of your asks; outline below and proposed next steps.

Summary answers (high level):
- BYOK: Yes — Redwood supports BYOK via customer-managed KMS. We support both cloud KMS keys (customer-managed in EU region) and HSM-backed keys for dedicated/private deployments. We do not require customer keys to be escrowed by default.
- Key escrow: Redwood’s standard position is no escrow. If a customer requests escrow for operational reasons we handle that as a case-by-case legal/ops exception with strict controls.
- Subprocessor notice: We can agree to a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors for enterprise contracts.
- Transfers: We can execute SCCs and also offer contractual safeguards in the DPA.
- Evidence: We will provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a pen test summary redacted for sensitive details.

Technical/ops items to confirm before final TOMs wording:
- Where in the customer workflow is data stored and for how long (retention window)?
- Expected traffic/throughput (this affects whether we recommend caching vs. per-request encryption isolation).
- Do you require absolute no-cache for any classes of PII?

Attachments: I’ve attached our internal TOMs draft focused on BYOK and KMS options (Redwood_TOMs_BYOK_options.pdf) and a short checklist for the call.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-minute call this week with Jane + Marcus + Monica (Security) + Aditya (Legal ops) to align technical scope.
2) Redwood to propose specific DPA redlines post-call and route DocuSign envelope for execution.
3) Security will provide SOC 2 under NDA and pen test summary within 3 business days after call.

I’m available 11:00–13:00 PT Wed or Thu. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

- If we accept 30-day subprocessor notice, procurement will require a clause for emergency rapid onboarding (e.g., 72-hour exception with written notice) — call out as an exception in the DPA.
- For BYOK: operationally we need to capture the key rotation schedule and whether the customer will rotate keys without impacting running workloads. Suggest a sentence under the TOMs on rotation coordination and API for revocation.
- E-signature: Acme prefers DocuSign. Please ensure the envelope has the right corporate signatory block (I’ll provide the internal template).

Also looping in Monica for technical confirmation on cache isolation and logging.

Marcus / team —

Thanks for the speedy response and for the TOMs draft. A few clarifications from Acme Security/Legal after review:

- Subprocessor notice: we will accept the 30-day notice. Please add language that requires Redwood to provide a mechanism for customers to request termination of subprocessor processing for their data within 30 days if a risk is identified.
- Key escrow: Acme will not accept any form of vendor-side key escrow. Please update the TOMs to explicitly state Redwood will not store customer key material.
- EU KMS: we require the option to provision keys within eu-west-1 (or equivalent) and to prevent egress of keys outside the region.
- Exports & transfers: SCCs acceptable. Please confirm whether you support a transfer-impact assessment for any subprocessors that process data outside the EEA.
- Evidence: We will need SOC 2 Type II (latest) and confirmation of encryption in transit+at rest with algorithm names (e.g., TLS1.3, AES-256-GCM).

I’ve attached an annotated TOMs file with inline comments (Acme_TOMs_annotated.pdf). For speed, I’m also sending a DocuSign envelope that contains our preferred DPA redline; envelope id is 0a1b2c3d4e5f. The envelope requests signatures from both parties — please confirm Redwood’s signatory and whether the envelope can be modified to remove escrow language prior to signing.

Appreciate the help — looking to get this into sign next week.

-jane

Jane —

Appreciate the annotated TOMs and the DocuSign envelope. Confirmations and next steps below:

Confirmations:
- Subprocessor: Redwood will provide 30 days’ notice. We will add an express clause in the DPA that allows the customer to request cessation of processing for their account-specific data if a material risk is identified; requests will be handled under the incident/process described in the DPA.
- Key escrow: Redwood does not hold customer key material. We will add explicit wording in the TOMs: "Redwood will not retain or escrow customer unmanaged key material."
- EU KMS & regional restrictions: We support keys provisioned in customer-selected EU regions (e.g., eu-west-1). We will include a statement that keys will not be transferred outside the selected region unless the customer instructs otherwise in writing.
- Transfers & subprocessors: Redwood performs transfer-impact assessments for subprocessors that will process data outside the EEA and will provide summary findings to customers upon request (sensitive detail redacted).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report will be shared under NDA; encryption algorithms: TLS 1.3 for in-transit, AES-256-GCM for at-rest by default.

DocuSign envelope: We reviewed the envelope. We will accept DocuSign for execution but need two changes before signing: (1) remove the escrow language from the DPA and (2) add Redwood’s standard operational exception language for emergency subprocessors (72-hr escalation path). Aditya, can you coordinate the redline to the envelope?

Proposed mutual action plan:
- Today (Thu): Aditya to propose the two redlines and update the DocuSign envelope.
- Fri (1 business day): Acme to confirm redline.
- Next Tue: Security to upload SOC 2 under NDA; legal to finalize DPA.
- Within 3 business days of signed DPA: Redwood will start the TOMs implementation checklist.

Signatory: Redwood signatory will be Marcus Lin (Head of Sales) for the SOW/DPA side; legal countersignatory will be Aditya Rao for contracts.

If that looks good I’ll ask Security to prepare the SOC 2 package and we’ll route the revised envelope.

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
